name: grp-mcp
description: Drive an Acumatica ERP instance from Claude: read, write, run processes and diagnose failures across the five APIs Acumatica actually has. Talks to your own instance directly - nothing is proxied, and credentials never leave your machine. Writes are off per profile until you enable them, and a clean 'ok' is never trusted: writes are read back and anything unconfirmed is reported as unverified. Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux from PyPI through uvx, so it needs uv installed - 'winget install astral-sh.uv' on Windows, 'brew install uv' on a Mac. Run tools\Edit-Connections.cmd once to create your connections file; it lands in %USERPROFILE%\grp-mcp (~/.grp-mcp on macOS and Linux), outside AppData where a Claude app update cannot delete it, and the server finds it with no environment variable set. LATEST (0.81.0-rc34): six ways a write or a delete reported the wrong outcome. A delete your profile forbids could still happen - the diagnostic replay ran under the write permission rather than the delete one, so a write-without-delete profile had a delete path it was configured to forbid. A segmented key you asked to delete could be reported deleted while it was still there, because the tables consulted to check answer empty on some instances; it now confirms on a plane that can actually see the record, and says 'cannot confirm' rather than 'absent' when nothing can. A committed import could report that it committed nothing - the per-row flags lag the run status, and one read caught them all false while the records existed. Import scenarios silently dropped '=' formulas on any screen with a lookup key field, storing a mangled value and reporting success. A delete could be confirmed against a different record, because some screens jump elsewhere after saving. And classic screens that page through records instead of jumping to one by key - Segmented Keys among them - were unreachable to every classic-plane tool; they now work, which also makes a multi-segment key deletable for the first time. Full history in docs/CHANGELOG.md.
